name: Textarea
summary: Lets people enter or edit several lines of text.
description: A textarea collects free text that may run over several lines: a message, a description, a comment, an address. It shows a chosen number of lines, scrolls beyond them and can be resized. It has a visible label above, an optional description and, when its value fails validation, a message under it. One line of text is a Text field.

anatomy.description: Root. Stacks the label, the control, the description and the message; carries the size and the forced state.
Text naming the field. Provides the accessible name; activating it focuses the control.

The required mark of the Forms rule, at the end of the label after a word space: "(optional)" on a field that is not required when the form marks optional fields, "(required)" on a required field when it marks required fields (markedFields), nothing otherwise. The label's size, regular, the description's color (decision mark-style). On the web "(required)" is hidden from assistive technology, the required attribute saying it, and "(optional)" is part of the name.

On Android and Windows only, in place of the mark: an asterisk at the end of the label of a required field, 4 px after it (2 px in small), at the label's size and weight (label.typography), in the error message's red (decision asterisk-style), kept in the accessible name. Never drawn on the web, iOS and macOS, so neither the reference rendering nor the Figma component draws it.
The editable box: the native multi-line text control, drawn by the component. Receives focus, holds the value, shows the placeholder while empty and as many lines as the rows property.
Optional help text under the control (format, example, consequence), associated with it as its description.

Text saying what the severity means (what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check, what was confirmed), under the description (under the control when there is none), associated with the control as a description, after it. Shown only with a severity; the description stays.

Glyph of the icon font saying the severity, named after it ("Error", "Warning", "Success"): error, warning or check_circle, the Alert's glyphs. Placed by severityIcon: after the control, centred on it, the control giving up its size and gap; or at the start of the message, before its text. Never inside the control, where browsers add their own elements.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Control height, value text and inline padding take the height, the text size and the inline padding of the Button of the same size; the label takes the text size of the value; the description and the message take the helper sizes.

options.description: Dense forms, toolbars, table rows (28 px high).
Prominent, single fields: a search page, a sign-in form (44 px).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What the field asks for, as a noun phrase (Email address). Always visible.

properties.name: Placeholder
properties.description: Short hint shown while the field is empty, in a lighter color. It disappears when people type: never the label, never an instruction people must remember.

properties.name: Rows
properties.description: Number of text lines visible before the control scrolls; people can resize it vertically.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text: expected format, example, or what the value is used for.

properties.name: Message
properties.description: What the severity means: what is wrong and how to fix it, what to check, or what was confirmed. Shown with a severity, in the color of that severity, and replaces errorMessage.

properties.name: Severity icon
properties.description: Where the severity icon goes. A rule of the form, not of the field: a form sets it once, to the same value, for all its controls (Forms decision forms-severity-icon-placement).

options.description: At the start of the message, before its text, 16 px; the control keeps its full width (default).
After the control, centred on it, at the size of the Button's icon of the same size; the control gives up the icon and the gap.
No icon: the message says the severity in words ("Error: …").

properties.name: Marked fields
properties.description: Which fields carry the required mark. A rule of the form, not of the field: a form sets it once, to the same value, for all its controls (Forms decision forms-marked-fields); the field draws its mark from its own required.

options.description: "(optional)" on the field when it is not required, nothing when it is (default). The form says once, before its first field, "All fields are required unless marked optional.".
"(required)" on the field when it is required, nothing when it is not: for a form where most fields are optional.
No mark: a field outside a form, such as a table's filter or a setting applied at once.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: The field must be filled to submit the form. It draws the mark that markedFields asks for ("(required)" on a required field, "(optional)" on one that is not), and the asterisk on Android and Windows.

properties.name: Read-only
properties.description: The value can be read, focused and copied but not edited (a generated identifier). Say so in the label or the description.

properties.name: Severity
properties.description: What the check of the value found. Replaces the invalid boolean: error, warning and success are the three severities of a form control (decision forms-severity); information that holds before any check is the description's job.

options.description: No severity: nothing was checked, or there is nothing to say (default).
The value is not accepted: the border takes the error color, the message says what is wrong and how to fix it, and the control is exposed as in error (aria-invalid on the web).
The value is accepted but deserves attention: the border takes the warning color and the message says what to check. No web state: said in the message text.
The value was checked and confirmed: the border takes the success color and the message says what was confirmed. No web state: said in the message text.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Non-interactive and skipped by the keyboard; the value stays visible. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.

states.description: Resting: an outlined box on the default surface.
Pointer over the control. The box takes the surface hover tint; the border does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.

Focus on the control, from the keyboard or a pointer: an editable field shows the focus color as a 2.4 px outline drawn flush over its border however it was focused; the border and the text do not move.

Severity error: the box is filled with the subtle error background, on hover too, an outline in the error color is drawn flush over the border (1.2 px at rest, 2.4 px with focus) and the message is shown under the control, in the error color.

Severity warning: the box is filled with the subtle warning background, on hover too, an outline in the warning color is drawn flush over the border (1.2 px at rest, 2.4 px with focus) and the message is shown under the control, in the warning color. No web state beyond the data attribute.

Severity success: the box is filled with the subtle success background, on hover too, an outline in the success color is drawn flush over the border (1.2 px at rest, 2.4 px with focus) and the message is shown under the control, in the success color. No web state beyond the data attribute.
Not editable: the box takes the level 1 surface; the value stays focusable and selectable.
Non-interactive. Box, value, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors; hover and focus do not apply.

notes: Label, control, description and message stack, separated by container.gap; the control fills the width of the component, which the layout sizes.

Inline padding, minimum height and text size come from the size option; the corner radius (2 px at small, 4 px at medium and large, as the Button's) comes from it too; the border width does not change.
The block padding sets the inset of the first and last lines; the control grows with the rows property and can be resized vertically.
With severityIcon after-control and a severity that has an icon, the control and the icon share a row: the control fills it, the icon follows at severity-icon.gap.

When people raise the text size the lines grow and the control grows with them, keeping its own block padding (control.padding-block, 6 / 8 / 12 px) above and below the text (decision grows-with-text-size).

name.text: Computed from the label, associated with the control as its label element on the web. The description and the message are exposed as the accessible description, not as part of the name. The placeholder is exposed as a placeholder and used as a name only when nothing else names the control, which never happens here.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the control. A disabled control is not focusable and is skipped.
Inserts a new line in this multi-line edit control.
On iPadOS 15 and later with a hardware keyboard, moves focus among focus groups, the field included: iPadOS supports keyboard navigation in text fields and text views.
Goes into the text of the text view, which edits multi-line text; the submit action is triggered by text fields and secure fields only.
Inserts a tab character, the platform's default in a multi-line field; Shift+Tab and the arrow keys leave the field, so focus is not trapped.
Moves focus to the previous focus target.
Move the caret; at the start or the end of the text (on the first or the last line) they move focus to the adjacent focus target.
Select characters, select all: the system handles them for a text field with a hardware keyboard.
Inserts a new line: only a single-line field refuses new lines.
On macOS, move focus to the next or the previous view of the key view loop.
On macOS, selects all the characters in the field.
On Windows, moves focus in the tab order, which follows the order the controls are added; a disabled field is removed from it.
On Windows, moves focus in reverse tab order.
On Windows, move the caret inside the field: in a text field every key goes to entering or navigating the text first.
On Windows, inserts a new line: the Textarea's text box sets AcceptsReturn, which lets it take newline characters.

guidelines.text: Expose the textbox role, the name, the value and the required, read-only, disabled and error states through the platform's native multi-line text control, so assistive technology receives them without extra work.
Use the native textarea element: it exposes the textbox role as multi-line, with its value and states, without ARIA.
Every field has a visible label associated with the control programmatically; help text that people need to fill the field (format, example) is visible too, as the description.
Associate the label with a label element whose for attribute names the control's id; reference the description and the message with aria-describedby, so they are read after the name.
The placeholder is a short hint, never the label and never an instruction: it disappears as soon as people type, and is not exposed as the name when a label exists.
Show a hint in a text field to help communicate its purpose; because placeholder text disappears when people start typing, include a separate label describing the field.
Apple's recommended minimum text size is 11 pt on iOS and iPadOS; the description (12 pt at its smallest) and the message (14 pt at its smallest) are above it.

Say the severity in text next to the field, whatever it is: the message names what is wrong and how to fix it for an error, what to check for a warning and what was confirmed for a success, and is associated with the control. Color is never the only sign of a severity.

Say that the value is in error with aria-invalid="true" on the control, for the error severity only, and that a field is required with the required attribute, which the browser exposes as required. The web has no state for a warning or a success: the message says them, and aria-invalid is never set for them.
Mark required fields in the label or the description, never by the error color alone.

Label, value, description and message text contrast at least 4.5:1 with their background in every color mode and enabled state: label and value 19.03:1 (light) and 11.28:1 (dark) on the default surface, description 12.78:1 and 8.86:1, placeholder 6.08:1 and 6.40:1, message text in its severity color: error 6.12:1 and 7.06:1, warning 6.49:1 and 11.17:1, success 7.87:1 and 7.89:1 (on every surface level the lowest are error 5.79:1 in light mode and 5.30:1 in dark mode, warning 6.16:1 and 8.38:1, success 7.44:1 and 5.92:1). On the severity fills (global.bg.subtle.functional.<severity>.default, at rest and on hover), the value is at least 16.91:1 (light) and 11.43:1 (dark) and the placeholder 5.42:1 and 6.48:1: error 16.91 / 11.67:1 and 5.42 / 6.62:1, warning 17.15 / 11.54:1 and 5.50 / 6.55:1, success 17.30 / 11.43:1 and 5.55 / 6.48:1. Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

The border is what identifies the field, so it contrasts at least 3:1 with the adjacent surface in every color mode: 3.30:1 (light) and 6.40:1 (dark) on the default surface at rest (3.12:1 and 4.80:1 at the lowest, on the surface levels 1 and 3 in light mode and level 3 in dark), 3.12:1 and 5.86:1 against the hover fill on the default surface; the severity borders and outlines (the accent functional border): error 6.12:1 and 4.97:1, warning 6.49:1 and 8.09:1, success 7.87:1 and 6.08:1 on the default surface, and at least 5.79:1 and 3.73:1 (error), 6.16:1 and 6.07:1 (warning), 7.44:1 and 4.57:1 (success) on every surface level; the focus outline 5.77:1 and 12.76:1. The outlines are drawn over the border, on the surface around the field, so they are checked against it. Against the error fill, the other color next to it, the error border is 5.45:1 (light) and 5.14:1 (dark). Disabled is exempt. Against the warning fill the warning border is 5.86:1 in light mode and 8.27:1 in dark mode; against the success fill the success border is 7.17:1 and 6.16:1.

The field can be reached, edited and left from a keyboard, physical or assistive, on every platform, through the platform's native text control and its keyboard services, and focus is never trapped in it; the keys are the platform's.
Use the native text view so Full Keyboard Access reaches it, and test the app with Full Keyboard Access on. Unlike buttons, text fields and text views have keyboard navigation on iPadOS.

With a hardware keyboard, a D-pad or Switch Access, focus navigation reaches the field and highlights it, in a logical order, and focus can always move away from it: by default Compose does not trap focus in a text field.
On macOS, Full Keyboard Access lets people navigate to the field and use it with the keyboard alone: use the native control and keep the standard keyboard shortcuts.
Enter adds a line in the Textarea on every platform, so its return key keeps the platform's default label for a new line (enter on the web); the form does not set it.

A visible focus indicator appears when the control receives focus: a 2.4 px outline in the focus color drawn flush over the border, at every size, so focus is visible by pointer and keyboard alike (WCAG 2.4.7). WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA) is not met at 1x and 2x, because the part of the outline over the border changes contrast only 2.21:1 in light and 1.13:1 in dark, and the fields do not claim it.

The focus outline is drawn with :focus-visible, which browsers match whenever an editable field has focus, pointer or keyboard. It is a CSS outline, never a box-shadow, so forced colors mode repaints it in a system color.

The severity outline (1.2 px) and the focus outline (2.4 px) differ by width, so a field with a severity is not mistaken for a focused one, in forced colors too, where both take the same system color. At 1x the severity outline is as wide as the 1 px border at rest: the severity's color and the message say what the severity is, never the color alone.
Every size is a pointer target of at least 24 x 24 CSS pixels through its minimum height: 28, 36 and 44 pixels.

The label, description and message are set from 12 to 16 px (the message from 14), under the large text size of the contrast criterion (18 pt, about 24 px), so their colors keep 4.5:1. WCAG sets no minimum text size: it asks that text resize up to 200 % without loss of content or functionality, which the box allows because its height is a minimum that grows with larger text and keeps its block padding.
Text sizes are px lengths today, which a browser's text-only size setting does not change: zoom enlarges the text and the box together, which meets Resize Text.
The text grows with Dynamic Type, up to the larger accessibility sizes, and the box grows with its lines and keeps its own block padding, as Apple asks that layouts adapt to all font sizes.
macOS does not support Dynamic Type: on macOS, the field keeps its size, as text does.
On Windows, people can enlarge text alone up to 225 %, and controls and containers must resize with it: the box grows with its lines and keeps its own block padding.

Fields that collect information about the person (name, email, phone, address) carry the matching autocomplete token, so browsers and assistive technology can identify their purpose. The template passes it through its extra attributes.
A read-only field keeps its value focusable and selectable and is exposed as read-only; a disabled field leaves the focus order. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.

A read-only field looks almost the same as an editable one (its fill is 1.05:1 in light and 1.09:1 in dark from the resting fill, the same as the hover fill): say that it is read-only in the label or the description, not by the fill alone.

Apple's default control size on iOS is 44 x 44 pt, and every size has a hit region of at least that: the small and medium boxes (28 and 36 pt high) keep their drawn size and the hit region extends 8 and 4 pt above and below them, centered, over its own label, description and message, which keep their 6 pt; the layout keeps it clear of other controls and of another field's label. The large box (44 pt) is the hit region.

Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp, and every size reaches it without growing: the box (28, 36 or 44 dp high) keeps its drawn size and its touch target extends 10, 6 or 2 dp above and below it, centered, over its own label, description and message, which keep their 6 dp; the layout keeps it clear of other controls and of another field's label. Compose extends a small clickable's touch target outside its bounds by itself, so the box does not take the minimumInteractiveComponentSize modifier, which would reserve that space and move the label. Expose an error with the error semantics so the message is announced with the field.
Color transitions of the control are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

The severity icon is named after the severity ("Error", "Warning", "Success") and is part of the field's description: at the start of the message it is inside the message, which aria-describedby references; after the control, aria-describedby references it too, before the message, so the description reads "Error" and then the message. It is never the only cue: the message says what is wrong. The icon reaches 3:1 on every surface level (at the lowest: error 5.81:1 light, 5.30:1 dark; warning 6.16:1 and 8.38:1; success 7.44:1 and 5.92:1).

Hide "(required)" with aria-hidden="true": the required attribute says the field is required, once. "(optional)" stays in the label element, so the name ends with it ("Company (optional)"): no attribute says that a field is optional. The visible label still starts with the name, so speech input by the label works.

decisions.text: The textarea grows with the text size as the Text field does (decision grows-with-text-size of the Text field, which holds the rule and the options rejected): its lines grow with the text, so the box grows with them, and it keeps its own block padding (space.6 / 8 / 12, decision rows-and-resize), larger than the field family's minimum (space.3 / 5 / 8), above and below the lines; its minimum height stays 28 / 36 / 44. pnpm validate compares every other token with the Text field's and lets control.padding-block differ (scripts/lib/mirrors.mjs, differs). Where nothing scales the text (macOS), and on the web, where zoom scales text and box together, the textarea keeps its size.

Enter (Return) adds a line in the Textarea on every platform, as a multi-line edit control; the return key keeps the platform's default label for a new line, and the form does not set it. A single-line field passes Enter to the form instead (the Forms foundation says what the form does).

Being reached, edited and left from a keyboard is a requirement on every platform (WCAG 2.1.1 on the web, EN 301 549 11.2.1.1.1 for native software), met, as on the Button, through the platform's native text control and its keyboard services, and focus is never trapped in the field (WCAG 2.1.2). Unlike the Button, the keys are named on every platform whose own documentation names them for text entry: Tab on the web; on iPadOS, Tab among focus groups (iPadOS supports keyboard navigation in text fields and text views, so the Button's line against keyboard navigation of one's own is not carried) and Full Keyboard Access; on Android, Shift+Tab back, the arrow keys and the D-pad moving the caret then leaving at the edge of the text, the system's selection keys, and on Android Tab inserts a tab character in this multi-line field, the platform's default, and Shift+Tab and the arrow keys leave it; on macOS, Tab and Shift-Tab through the key view loop and Command-A; on Windows, the tab order, Shift+Tab and the arrow keys moving the caret. Each platform keeps its own behaviour. Three prefixes join the trusted sources for it: Android Developers' Compose focus and keyboard pages (develop/ui/compose/touch-input/) and text pages (develop/ui/compose/text/), and Windows' input pages (windows/apps/develop/input/).

As on the Button, on iOS and Android every size reaches the platform's touch target without growing: the hit region is at least 44 x 44 pt on iOS and 48 x 48 dp on Android, centered on the box. It may extend over its own label, description and message, which are not targets, so the 6 px between the parts stays on every platform; the layout keeps it clear of every other control and of another field's label. Above and below the box it extends 8, 4 and 0 pt on iOS and 10, 6 and 2 dp on Android at the small, medium and large sizes. A Textarea whose rows make its box at least as tall as the target (the default 3 rows at every size) needs no overhang in height. On Android, Compose extends a small clickable's touch target outside its bounds by itself; the box does not take minimumInteractiveComponentSize, which would reserve the space around it and move the label. The drawn field, its parts and its tokens stay the same on every platform, as in Figma; the web (WCAG 2.5.8, 24 x 24 CSS px) and desktop already meet their targets with the box.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 18, point 1) among: A, the Button's rule as is, the hit region reserved all around the box (on iOS and Android the label would sit 14, 10 and 6 pt or 16, 12 and 8 dp from the box instead of 6, unlike the web and Figma); B, the hit region over the field's own text, reserved only against other controls and other fields' labels (recommended, chosen); C, the whole field as the target, a tap on the label or the help text focusing the field (no platform documents it, and selecting text in a description would focus the field); D, platform heights of 44 pt and 48 dp (a semantic addition; the three sizes would look the same on mobile and no longer line up with the Button, undoing box-height-button there). No trusted source says that tapping a field's label focuses it on iOS or Android, so the label does not count as part of the target. Measured on the review sheet: with 16 px between fields nothing has to be kept; with none, the next small field is kept 8 pt (iOS) or 10 dp (Android) lower; a small Search field 8 px above navigation items keeps 2 dp more on Android.

decisions.text: The Textarea draws the required mark as the mark part, inside the label after a word space, and keeps the asterisk part for Android and Windows. The web template takes markedFields (optional by default) and markLabel, to translate the words; "(required)" is aria-hidden. In Figma the component draws the web rendering only: a BOOLEAN "Mark" (on by default) shows the mark, whose TEXT "Mark text" is "(optional)" and is typed "(required)" when the form marks required fields; markedFields is not a variant axis and the asterisk is not drawn. Tokens: mark.color.* and mark.typography.* (mark-style); asterisk.color.* and asterisk.margin-inline-start.* (asterisk-style), the asterisk taking label.typography.*.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 16, point 4) among: A, a BOOLEAN and a TEXT for the mark and a BOOLEAN for the asterisk, markedFields kept out of the variant axes (recommended); B, markedFields and required as variant axes, six times the variants (6912 for the Text field); C, the Figma prototype's single BOOLEAN drawing the asterisk, the words typed into the label. The team chose A without the asterisk: the Figma components draw the current web specification, not every platform's rendering, so Figma shows "(optional)", "(required)" or no mark, never the asterisk. Variant counts are unchanged (Text field 1152, Number field 1152, Textarea 576, Search field 24). Departs from the Figma prototype, whose BOOLEAN "required" (on by default) draws a red asterisk. The word space before the mark is a quarter of the font size in Figma (3.5 px at 14 px, 4 px at 16 px), as measured on the web.

decisions.text: On Windows, a required Textarea keeps its asterisk in its accessible name: the UI Automation Name is the label as shown ("Full name*"), and the control sets AutomationProperties.IsRequiredForForm. The words keep their exposure on the other platforms (hidden on the web and macOS, read on iOS).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 16, point 3b) among: A, hide the asterisk from Narrator and let IsRequiredForForm alone say required; B, keep it in the Name (chosen, recommended). The team asked to follow the Windows recommendation for Windows specificities: Microsoft asks that the UI Automation Name be the label on screen, not a modified version of it, and no Microsoft page says Narrator announces IsRequiredForForm, so A could leave required unsaid while B at worst says it twice. Applies the Forms decision forms-required-windows-name, which cites the UI Automation property identifiers and Windows' accessible name guidance.

decisions.text: On Android and Windows, the Textarea marks a required field with an asterisk at the end of its label, whatever markedFields says when it is optional or required (nothing with none), and draws nothing on an optional field. The asterisk is the color of the error message and of the error icon (global.text.on-base.functional.error.default), at the label's size and weight (14 / 16 / 16 px, medium), 4 px after the label (2 px in small), with no word space; disabled, the label's disabled color (global.text.state.disabled.default). 5.79 to 6.12:1 in light mode, 5.30 to 7.06:1 in dark mode on levels 0 to 3. The words of the other platforms keep mark-style.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 16, point 3) among: A, the mark's own look (mark-style; recommended); B, the label's style; C, the Figma prototype's red asterisk (chosen). The team chose C because a reddish asterisk is the most common rendering of a required field in interfaces, and asked that its red be the color of the severity message and of the severity icon. Applies the Forms decision forms-asterisk-style. Matches the Figma prototype on Android and Windows (its asterisk, color, weight and gap); the words of the web, iOS and macOS stay a departure. The asterisk gets its own tokens (component tokens are never forked per platform), which land with point 4.

decisions.text: The Textarea's required mark ("(optional)" or "(required)", from marked-fields) follows the label's text after a word space, at the label's size (14 / 16 / 16 px for small, medium, large), in the regular weight (body.weight.regular) and the description's color (global.text.on-base.neutral.secondary); disabled, the label's disabled color (global.text.state.disabled.default). 12.09 to 12.78:1 in light mode, 6.65 to 8.86:1 in dark mode on levels 0 to 3.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 16, point 2) among: the Figma prototype's red asterisk (reference: global.text.on-base.functional.error.default, the label's size and weight, 4 px after it, 2 px in small); A, the label's own style; B, the label's size, regular, the description's color (chosen, recommended); C, the label's size and color, regular; D, the description's style (12 / 12 / 14 px). The team hesitated between B and D and chose B: a smaller mark, the only element of a different size, draws the eye before the label itself. Applies the Forms decision forms-mark-style. The word space measures 3.5 px at 14 px and 4.0 px at 16 px, near Figma's 4 px. Departs from Figma (red asterisk). The tokens (mark.color.*, mark.typography.*) land with point 4.

decisions.text: The Textarea draws the required mark of the Forms rule from a form setting: it carries markedFields (optional, required, none; optional by default), which a form sets once, to the same value, for all its controls, and draws its mark from its own required: "(optional)" when it is not required and the form marks optional fields, "(required)" when it is required and the form marks required fields, nothing with none. A required textarea never says "(optional)". none is for a field outside a form, such as a table's filter or a setting applied at once.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 16, point 1) among: A, a form setting, optional by default (chosen, recommended); B, the same setting, none by default; C, a mark chosen per field, nothing tying it to required; D, no property, the words typed into the label. Applies the Forms decision forms-marked-fields: a form that sets nothing follows the Forms rule (forms-required-marking), a mark can never contradict required, and on the web "(required)" can stay hidden from assistive technology (forms-required-mark-exposure) while Android and Windows swap it for their asterisk (forms-required-marking-platforms). The Figma prototype marks each required field with a red asterisk, shown by default: a departure. The mark's look, the platforms' asterisk and the part, its tokens and the Figma axis are #103 step 16, points 2 to 4.

decisions.text: The Textarea shows a visible label (above the control by default, Forms rule label-placement), the control, the description under it when there is one and, while a severity shows, the message under the description (under the control when there is no description), for every severity: the description stays visible while a message shows. The control's description lists the description, then the message; on the web aria-describedby references them in that order, with the severity icon's name before the message when the icon is after the control. This applies the Forms foundation's decision forms-message-under-description and departs from the Figma prototype, where the error, warning or success message takes the place of the helper text.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 14) among: A, keep the message under the description (chosen); B, Figma's anatomy, the message replacing the description while a severity shows. A keeps the help (a format, a limit) on the screen and in what assistive technology reads when people fix the value: AccName concatenates every node aria-describedby references, so a screen reader reads the description, then the message. B would reopen the Forms rule and does not even keep the height: since decision message-text-size the message (14 / 16 / 16 px) is larger than the description (12 / 12 / 14 px), so a medium field with a one-line description still grows 6 px when the message replaces it, and 30 px with no description, while the help disappears. Measured on 320 px wide fields: a one-line message adds 30 px under a medium field (the 6 px gap and a 24 px line), a two-line message 48 px under a small one; both parts keep their size, weight and color, 6 px apart (container.gap). Supersedes label-description-error, whose text still named the error message and the invalid state. No token, CSS, template, Figma blueprint or theme change; the error example gains a description, so the docs show both parts together.

decisions.text: The border and outline of a field with a warning keep textarea.control.border-color.warning and textarea.control.outline-color.warning, global.border.accent.functional.warning.default, which the Color foundation sets in light mode to the warning text's step, warning 600 (#765818; decision border-accent-warning-600): the warning's border, outline, icon and message read one color, as the error's and the success's do, and every pair of the warning and success rendering passes WCAG 2.2 AA in both modes. No component token changes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 13, point 4, the closing WCAG check of the warning and success rendering, also the Forms foundation step 6, forms-warning-border-600) between: A, close as landed, the light warning border at warning 500 (2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, under the 3:1 of WCAG 1.4.11, issue #119); B, the light warning border at its text step, warning 600 (chosen), as the error and success borders take their text's step. Every other pair of the warning and success rendering passed (measured on the Text field, the Number field and the Textarea, light and dark, levels 0 to 3). With B the warning border and outline are 6.49 / 6.16 / 6.49 / 6.16:1 on the light levels (was 3.27 / 3.09:1) and 5.86:1 on the warning fill (was 2.95:1); dark mode unchanged (8.27:1 on its fill, 6.07:1 at the lowest).

decisions.text: The warning severity icon and the warning message read one color, as the error's and the success's do: the tokens keep their roles (textarea.severity-icon.color.warning, global.icon.on-base.functional.warning.default; textarea.message.color.warning, global.text.on-base.functional.warning.default), and the Color foundation maps the warning icon role to the warning text, warning 600 (#765818) in light mode and warning 300 (#FFC61C) in dark mode (decision warning-on-base-600). No component token changes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 13, point 3, also the Forms foundation step 6, forms-warning-one-color) among: A, keep the two roles as the Figma library maps them in light mode (icon warning 500 #BD8107, message warning 800 #3E2D0C, 3.97:1 apart); B, the warning icon in the text color; C, the message in the icon color (3.09:1, under the 4.5:1 of WCAG 1.4.3); D, the message at warning 600 with the icon at 500; F, the message at warning 600 and the icon in the same color (chosen); E, the message on the on-subtle text role. The team asked that the warning work like the error and the success, whose icon role aliases their text role: the Color foundation's decision warning-on-base-600 maps the warning text to warning 600, the lightest step that passes 4.5:1, and the warning icon role to the warning text. Measured on the Text field (every size, both icon placements, light and dark, levels 0 to 3): icon and message 6.49 / 6.16 / 6.49 / 6.16:1 in light mode (the message was 13.02 / 12.36:1, the icon 3.27 / 3.09:1), 11.17 / 10.23 / 9.36 / 8.38:1 in dark mode, unchanged.

decisions.text: The severity icon is drawn for every severity: error for an error, warning for a warning, check_circle for a success (the Alert's glyphs), named "Error", "Warning" or "Success" (severityIconLabel translates it), in the on-base icon role of its severity: textarea.severity-icon.color.warning (global.icon.on-base.functional.warning.default, #BD8107 in light mode, #FFC61C in dark mode) and textarea.severity-icon.color.success (global.icon.on-base.functional.success.default, #075D33 and #11C772). Its place and size do not change.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 13, point 2, also the Forms foundation step 6, forms-severity-icon-glyphs) among: A, the Alert's glyphs, warning and check_circle (chosen); B, a plain check for the success; C, no success icon. A is the Figma prototype's and the Alert's glyphs: the three severities differ by shape as well as color, and the message still says the severity in text (WCAG 1.4.1). B departs from the Alert and from Figma and reuses the Checkbox's glyph, thinner at 16 px; C draws icons on some fields and not others under one placement rule, and after the control a field would change width or keep an empty gap when it passes. The color follows the rule decided for the error (forms-severity-icon-color), the on-base icon role of the severity. Measured on the Text field (every size, both placements, light and dark, levels 0 to 3): the warning icon 3.09 to 3.27:1 in light mode and 8.38 to 11.17:1 in dark mode, the success icon 7.44 to 7.87:1 and 5.92 to 7.89:1 (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1).

decisions.text: The box of a field with a warning or a success is filled like the box in error, with the subtle functional background of its severity, at rest and on hover alike: global.bg.subtle.functional.warning.default (textarea.control.background.warning, #FFF1C7 in light mode, #1F1504 in dark mode) and global.bg.subtle.functional.success.default (textarea.control.background.success, #DBFAE6 and #011C16), under the severity border and outline. Read-only and disabled keep their own fills. The value, the placeholder, the label, the description and the message keep their colors.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-25 (#103 step 13, point 1, also the reference rendering of the Forms foundation step 6, forms-severity-fill) among three options, measured at every size, at rest, on hover and with focus, light and dark, surface levels 0 to 3: A, keep the page-level fill for warning and success, only the error tinted; B, the error's rule for every severity, the subtle fill of the severity at rest and on hover alike (chosen); C, the subtle fill at rest and its hover step on hover. B is the Figma prototype's fill (#FFF1C7, #DBFAE6) and one rule for the three severities. On the fills, light / dark: placeholder 5.50 / 6.55:1 (warning) and 5.55 / 6.48:1 (success), value 17.15 / 11.54:1 and 17.30 / 11.43:1 (WCAG 1.4.3); success border on its fill 7.17 / 6.16:1; the light warning border is 2.95:1 on its fill, the shortfall accepted in the Forms foundation step 5b (issue #119), and keeps 3.09:1 against the surface (WCAG 1.4.11). C would make the severities differ on hover and bring the light warning border to 2.66:1 on the hover fill.

decisions.text: The Textarea has no leading icon: the leading icon of the field family is for the single-line fields only (Text field, Number field, Search field).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-20 (#103 step 15, point 1) among: A, keep today (no leading icon, the Search field keeps its own glyph); B, an optional leading icon on the single-line fields, off by default (chosen); C, as B and the Textarea too; D, on by default with a generic glyph, as the Figma prototype's left icon. The team chose B for what the component offers and A for what it advises: the icon must be feasible and optional for designs that want a more precise rendering (a marketing page with a few fields, for example), but the default and the guideline for regular applications is no leading icon, the Search field's glyph being the known exception. D was rejected because a default glyph means nothing for most fields (sell on an email field) and "on unless switched off" is the opposite of the Button's leading icon; C because no source and no Figma variant shows an icon in a multi-line field. The icon is decorative: hidden from assistive technology, never the label, which stays visible text (WCAG 1.1.1, 3.3.2, 2.5.3). Material lists a leading icon as optional and Apple lets a text field show an image at its leading end; Windows draws none. Its size, color, gap and accessibility contract are #103 step 15, points 2 to 5, which add the property, the part and its tokens.

decisions.text: The message of an error keeps textarea.message.color.error, global.text.on-base.functional.error.default (#C01619 in light mode, #F88275 in dark mode), the color of the severity icon (Forms decision forms-message-color).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-20 (#103 step 12, point 3) among: A, keep the functional error text (chosen); B, the neutral primary text; C, the neutral secondary text, the description's color. A is the Figma prototype's color and the icon's, and sets the message apart from the description by its color too, which matters most with no icon. Measured on the surface levels 0 to 3: 5.81 to 6.12:1 in light mode, 5.30 to 7.06:1 in dark mode (WCAG 1.4.3).

decisions.text: The Textarea gets a severity icon (part severity-icon) and the property severityIcon (message by default, after-control, none), as the Forms foundation decided (forms-severity-icon-placement, -size, -color). At the start of the message it is 16 px (textarea.severity-icon.size.message: size.2), textarea.severity-icon.gap.message (space.4) before the text; after the control it is the size of the Button's icon at the same size (textarea.severity-icon.size.after-control.*: size.3, 4, 4), textarea.severity-icon.gap.after-control (space.8) after the control. Its color is textarea.severity-icon.color.error, global.icon.on-base.functional.error.default. Shown for the error; warning and success follow with step 13. It follows the Text field (decision same-box-as-text-field).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-20 in #103 step 12, points 2 (C with the team's precisions: both placements and none, one rule per form, choice controls in the message), 2b (A, the Button's icon size) and 2c (A, the on-base role, the message's color). Measured on the field family: after the control the box gives up 28 / 32 / 32 px; the icon is 5.81 to 6.12:1 in light mode and 5.30 to 7.06:1 in dark mode on the surface levels 0 to 3. The icon is named so that the severity is in text for assistive technology wherever it sits (AccName 1.2 computes the description from the referenced nodes, the icon's name included); the message keeps saying what is wrong, so the icon is never the only cue (WCAG 1.4.1).

decisions.text: The message takes the size of the label and the value (textarea.message.typography.*: body.size.sm, md, md, so 14 / 16 / 16 px for small, medium and large), no longer the description's (body.size.xs, xs, sm: 12 / 12 / 14 px). The description keeps its size; the weight (medium), the line height (normal, 1.5) and the letter spacing are unchanged. This replaces the message part of the decision label-help-text-sizes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-20 while reviewing #103 step 12, point 2b (the error icon's size): at 12 px the message was too small for what it carries, what is wrong and how to fix it. Next to 14 and 16 px text the icon in the message is Icon small (16 px), the Icon spec's size for body text. Contrast is unchanged (text 4.5:1, WCAG 1.4.3): the colors do not depend on the size. The box does not move: the message sits under it and the description.

decisions.text: The box of a field in error is filled with global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default (textarea.control.background.error): #FEECEA in light mode, #2B0B08 in dark mode, at rest and on hover alike, under the error border and outline. Read-only and disabled keep their own fills. The value, the placeholder, the label, the description and the message keep their colors. It follows the Text field (decision same-box-as-text-field).
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-20 (#103 step 12, point 1, also the reference rendering of the Forms foundation step 6) between two options, measured on every size, at rest, on hover and with focus, light and dark, surface levels 0 to 3: A, global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default at rest and its hover step global.bg.subtle.functional.error.hover on hover; B, the subtle error fill at rest and on hover alike (chosen). In light mode A's hover fill (#FCCDC6) brings the placeholder to 4.33:1, under the 4.5:1 of WCAG 1.4.3; with B every pair passes: placeholder 5.42:1 (light) and 6.62:1 (dark), value 16.91:1 and 11.67:1, the error border and outline against the fill 5.45:1 and 5.14:1, against the surface levels 5.79:1 and 3.73:1 at the lowest. The fill is solid, as the team validated in the Forms foundation step 5; the hover tint it gives up was 1.05:1 from rest, and the Figma prototype, whose error fill is the same #FEECEA, has no hover in error. The value and the placeholder keep their roles (global.text.on-base.neutral.primary and .tertiary): the on-subtle neutral role has a single step, which cannot tell the placeholder from the value.

decisions.text: The Textarea follows the Text field's decision variants-modeled-differently, which holds the departures from the Figma prototype, the measurements and the options: the `value` property instead of the `filled` state, the platform's caret, `severity` with `message`, the `description`, an always visible label, and read-only kept. It adds the same guideline: a read-only field looks almost the same as an editable one (1.05:1 in light and 1.09:1 in dark from the resting fill, the same as the hover fill), so say that it is read-only in the label or the description, not by the fill alone. The read-only example and the readonly property say so. No token changes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep the model and record; B, A plus the read-only guideline (chosen); C, read-only styled as rest, rejected because it would remove the only visual cue and is a breaking change. See the Text field's decision for the reasoning.

decisions.text: The placeholder of the Textarea is global.text.on-base.neutral.tertiary in every enabled state (textarea.control.placeholder-color.default) and global.text.state.disabled.default when disabled, as the Text field's (decision placeholder-tertiary of the Text field, which holds the rule, the options and the measurements). The decision keeps the values the control already had: no token changes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep tertiary in every enabled state (chosen); B, Figma's secondary at rest and tertiary on focus; C, secondary in every state, rejected because it is too close to the typed value and the same color as the help text. See the Text field's decision for the measurements.

decisions.text: The resting border of the box is global.border.base.neutral.5, as the Text field's (decision border-base-neutral-5 of the Text field, which holds the rule, the options and the measurements): #8C8C8C in light and #9C9C9C in dark, 3.30:1 and 6.40:1 on the page, 3.12:1 and 4.80:1 at the lowest on the surface levels. Hover and read-only keep it. Disabled, the focus outline and the severity outlines are unchanged.

The fill of the box of the Textarea is the page's own level, as the Text field's (decision fill-page-level of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): global.bg.level.0.default at rest, global.bg.level.0.hover on hover, global.bg.level.1.default when read-only. The decision keeps the values the box already had: no token changes. The disabled fill is not decided here.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep the page level (chosen); B, Figma's level 1; C, the default Button's translucent subtle fill, rejected because the placeholder fails WCAG 1.4.3 in dark. The fill does not identify the field, the border does. Every form control reads the same fill.

decisions.text: The Textarea draws focus and a severity as the Text field does (decision state-outline-flush of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): the border stays 0.6 px in every state and the outline is drawn flush over it, offset minus the border width, so the text never moves. Focus is an outline of focus.ring.width (2.4 px) in color.focus.ring; a severity (error, warning or success) at rest an outline of stroke-width.md (1.2 px) in the severity's border color; a severity with focus 2.4 px in the severity's color. textarea.control.outline-offset.focus-visible is removed. pnpm validate compares the shared tokens with the Text field's through the mirror check.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 (E4a at offset minus 0.6 px); see the Text field's decision for the options, the rationale and the known consequences (2.4.13 not met at 1x and 2x, a severity at 1 px at 1x, the focus color broken for a severity with focus).

decisions.text: The Textarea takes the corner radius of the Button of the same size, as the Text field's (decision radius-button of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 2 px, medium and large 4 px (textarea.control.border-radius per size). pnpm validate compares the shared tokens with the Text field's through the mirror check. Changes the single 4 px radius of the Figma-library import; everything else is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options (A, keep 4 px at every size; B, the Shape foundation's radius per size, chosen; C, 2 px at every size); see the Text field's decision for the rationale.

decisions.text: The parts of the Textarea are 6 px apart at every size and in every state (textarea.container.gap, space.4 to space.6), as the Text field's (decision part-gap-6 of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale). pnpm validate compares the shared tokens with the Text field's through the mirror check. Changes the 4 px gap of the Figma-library import; everything else is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options (A, keep 4 px; B and C, Figma's two inconsistent sets of gaps; D, 6 px everywhere, chosen); see the Text field's decision for the rationale.

decisions.text: The label of the Textarea takes the text size of the value, and the description and the message the helper sizes, as the Text field's (decision label-help-text-sizes of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): label small 14 px, medium 16 px, large 16 px; description and message small 12 px, medium 12 px, large 14 px. Each is a typography token per size. pnpm validate compares textarea.label.typography.*, textarea.description.typography.* and textarea.message.typography.* with the Text field's. Changes the single 14 px style that the decisions sizes and value-text-button-size state; everything else they state is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep the single 14 px style for the label, the description and the message; B, the label follows the field (14 / 16 / 16 px) and the help text stays 14 px; C, the label follows the field and the help text takes Figma's helper sizes (12 / 12 / 14 px), chosen; D, Figma's sizes (label 12 / 14 / 16 px, help text 12 / 12 / 14 px, compact line height), rejected because the label would be smaller than the value at the small size and the Typography foundation would need an exception. A label above a field reads at the field's own size, and the help text is secondary to what it describes.

decisions.text: The inline padding of the box of the Textarea is the inline padding of the Button without an icon, as the Text field's (decision padding-inline-button of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 8 px, medium 12 px, large 16 px. The block padding stays the Textarea's own. The decision keeps the values the box already had: no token changes.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among three options: A, keep the inline padding of the Button without an icon (8 / 12 / 16 px), chosen; B, Figma's 6 / 8 / 10 px; C, the Button's label-side padding (8 / 8 / 10 px), rejected here because it belongs to the question of a leading icon in the field. A field and a Button of the same size start their text at the same inset.

decisions.text: The minimum height of the Textarea takes the height of the Button of the same size, as the Text field's (decision box-height-button of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 28 px, medium 36 px, large 44 px. It is a floor under the rows: at the default three rows the control is taller (three lines and the block padding), so the minimum only governs a Textarea of one row or one resized smaller. pnpm validate compares textarea.control.min-height.* with the Text field's. The block padding and the rows stay the Textarea's own. Changes the 32 / 40 / 48 px minimum heights that the decisions sizes and value-text-button-size state; everything else they state is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep 32 / 40 / 48 px (one step taller than the Button of the same size); B, the Button's heights 28 / 36 / 44 px, chosen; C, the height Figma's padding gives with the new text (33.6 / 40 / 44 px), which matches neither the Button nor today's; D, Figma's heights rounded up (36 / 40 / 44 px). A field and a Button of the same size line up (a search field next to its button, a form row), and the large size reaches the 44 pt that Apple recommends. The hit region of the small and medium sizes is a later step, as for the Button.

decisions.text: The value and placeholder text of the Textarea takes the text size of the Button of the same size, as the Text field's (decision value-text-button-size of the Text field, which holds the rule and its rationale): small 14 px, medium 16 px, large 16 px, regular weight, normal letter spacing and the tight line height (1.2) of the Text field, which pnpm validate compares with textarea.control.typography.*. The block padding and the rows stay the Textarea's own. Supersedes sizes: the heights, inline padding, border, corners and the 14 px label, description and error message of that decision are unchanged here; only the text of the large size (20 to 16 px) and the line height (1.5 to 1.2) change.
decisions.rationale: Decided by the team on 2026-11-19 among four options: A, keep today's text (small 14, medium 16, large 20 px, line height 1.5: the large size breaks the rule); B, the Button's whole label style (medium weight, compact line height 1.0, tight letter spacing), rejected because people's content would look like a control label, descenders and accents would touch the line, and the Typography foundation would need an exception; C, the Button's text size with the Typography foundation's single-line style (regular weight, normal letter spacing, tight line height 1.2), chosen; D, the Button's text size with the line height 1.5, rejected because that line height is meant for running text. The Textarea, which holds several lines, takes the same 1.2 line height by team decision (step 3b, option A; rejected: B, its own line height 1.5, the foundation's running-text value), the mirror staying whole.

decisions.text: The Textarea always renders the same box as the Text field of the same size and state: height, inline padding, text, border, corners, colors, focus ring, label, description, message and motion are the Text field's, and only its block padding and its rows are its own. A Text field decision on any of these applies to the Textarea in the same change: pnpm validate fails when a Textarea token differs from the Text field token at the same place (MIRRORS in scripts/lib/mirrors.mjs, decision field-family-mirrors of the Text field). The mirror covers rendering only: a contract decision is asked for the Textarea too.
decisions.rationale: Nothing tied the three plain fields to the Text field: a decision on its box left them behind. Mirroring them lets every rendering step of the Text field refinement change the four in the same commit, and pnpm validate prove they agree, where the alternatives (the Text field alone, with a closing step per sibling or an issue for the others) leave the siblings out of step in between. The Select is not mirrored now: it gets its own step later, with the complex controls.

decisions.text: The control shows one of three severities, set by the severity property (none by default, error, warning, success): its border takes the severity's accent functional border color and the message, the message property shown only with a severity, takes the severity's functional text color. A message carries every severity, in the same part; severity replaces the invalid property and message replaces errorMessage. On the web the error is aria-invalid="true" (and :user-invalid when the browser validates) and the severity is also data-severity; warning and success have no web state and are said in the message text. The fill, the icon and the message wording of each severity are rendered in Forms step 6. The accent borders reach 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1); the light warning border is 2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, which step 6 may use as the fill, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).
decisions.rationale: The team validated the Forms foundation's three severities (decision forms-validation-severities) and named the property severity; "error" is the word every platform uses (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, Compose error semantics, Material error text), where "invalid" is the web's technical term. The clean break is deliberate: the packages are alpha and unreleased, and a deprecated alias would cost a schema field and support in the validator, the bridge and the templates. This amends decisions field-colors and label-description-error, whose text still says invalid and error message.

decisions.text: The control is a box on the default surface outlined in the accent neutral border color; hover tints it with the surface hover color and keeps the border; invalid takes the base error border; read-only takes the level 1 surface; disabled takes the shared disabled colors. Value text is primary, the placeholder tertiary, the description secondary, the error message the error text color.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library maps no color to form controls. The accent neutral border is the lightest neutral border that keeps 3:1 against the surface in both modes (WCAG 1.4.11); the hover tint reuses the surface's own hover step.

decisions.text: Three sizes from the Figma library's space and body scales: small (32 px high, 8 px inline padding, 14 px text), medium (40, 12, 16, the default) and large (48, 16, 20); the border is 0.6 px (stroke-width.sm) and the corners 4 px (corner-radius.xs) at every size; label, description and error message keep 14 px.

A field always has a visible label above the control; help text goes under the control as the description, and the error message under it while the field is invalid. Both are exposed as the control's description.
The textarea shows the number of lines of its rows property (three by default), with a block padding of 6, 8 or 12 px by size, and people can resize it vertically; it never resizes horizontally.

changelog.note: Decision grows-with-text-size (#103 step 20, point 1): the textarea grows with the text size and keeps its own block padding (6 / 8 / 12), larger than the field family's new minimum block padding (3 / 5 / 8); pnpm validate lets control.padding-block differ from the Text field's (scripts/lib/mirrors.mjs, differs). Platform guidelines for the web (zoom), iOS (Dynamic Type), macOS and Windows (text scaling). No token, CSS or rendering change; contrast unchanged.

Decision enter-by-field-kind (#103 step 19, point 2): Enter adds a line on every platform and the return key keeps its default label. Keyboard entries for Enter / Return per platform and a guideline. Text only: no token, CSS, template or rendering change; contrast unchanged.

Decision keyboard-on-every-platform (#103 step 19, point 1): keyboard access stated on every platform, with the keys each platform's own documentation names for text entry (iPadOS, Android, macOS, Windows) in the keyboard contract, and the generic, iOS, Android and macOS guidelines; Android Developers' Compose focus, keyboard and text pages and Windows' input pages join the trusted sources. Text only: no token, CSS, template or rendering change; contrast unchanged.

Decision touch-target-hit-region (#103 step 18, point 1): on iOS every size has a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt and on Android a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp, centered on the box, extending over the field's own text (its 6 px part gap kept) and kept clear of other controls and of other fields' labels; the drawn field is unchanged. The iOS and Android guidelines state how each size reaches the target instead of the shortfall. No token, CSS, template or rendering change; contrast unchanged.

Decision mark-part: the required mark lands (#103 step 16, point 4). Parts mark and asterisk (Android and Windows) inside the label; property markedFields (optional by default); tokens mark.color.*, mark.typography.*, asterisk.color.* and asterisk.margin-inline-start.*; the web template draws the mark, "(required)" aria-hidden, and takes markLabel to translate it; the Figma component gains the BOOLEAN "Mark" and the TEXT "Mark text", no variant axis, and never draws the asterisk.
Decision required-windows-name: on Windows the asterisk stays in the accessible name, with IsRequiredForForm (#103 step 16, point 3b). No token or rendering change.

Decision asterisk-style: on Android and Windows, the required asterisk in the error message's red (global.text.on-base.functional.error.default), the label's size and weight, 4 px after the label (2 px in small); 5.79 to 6.12:1 light, 5.30 to 7.06:1 dark (#103 step 16, point 3). No token or rendering change yet.

Decision mark-style: the required mark at the label's size, regular, in the description's color (global.text.on-base.neutral.secondary), the disabled text color when disabled; 12.09 to 12.78:1 light, 6.65 to 8.86:1 dark (#103 step 16, point 2). No token or rendering change yet.

Decision marked-fields: the form setting markedFields (optional by default) says which fields carry a mark; the field draws its mark from its own required (#103 step 16, point 1). No token or rendering change yet.

Decision message-under-description (keep, #103 step 14): the message sits under the description for every severity, both visible, and is read after it, as the Forms foundation decided (forms-message-under-description); a departure from the Figma prototype, where the message replaces the helper text. Supersedes label-description-error. The message part says where it sits; the error example gains a description. No token or rendering change.

Decision warning-border-text-step: the light warning border and outline are warning 600 #765818 through the Color foundation's decision border-accent-warning-600 (no component token changes): 6.49:1 on the default surface and 6.16:1 at the lowest (was 3.27:1 and 3.09:1), 5.86:1 on the warning fill (was 2.95:1, under 3:1); dark mode unchanged.

Decision warning-one-color: the warning icon and message read one color, warning 600 #765818 in light mode, through the Color foundation's decision warning-on-base-600 (no component token changes): the message 6.49:1 on the default surface and 6.16:1 at the lowest (was 13.01:1 and 12.30:1), the icon 6.16:1 at the lowest (was 3.09:1); dark mode unchanged (11.17:1 and 8.38:1).

Decision severity-icon-glyphs: the severity icon is drawn for a warning (warning, "Warning") and a success (check_circle, "Success") too, in the on-base icon role of the severity (new tokens severity-icon.color.warning and .success). Warning icon 3.09:1 (light) and 8.38:1 (dark) at the lowest on the surface levels, success 7.44:1 and 5.92:1.

Decision severity-fill-subtle: a field with a warning or a success is filled with the subtle background of its severity (new tokens control.background.warning and .success), at rest and on hover alike, as the error is; it kept the page-level fill before. Placeholder on the fills 5.50:1 and 5.55:1 (light), 6.55:1 and 6.48:1 (dark); value 17.15:1 and 17.30:1, 11.54:1 and 11.43:1; success border on its fill 7.17:1 and 6.16:1; the light warning border is 2.95:1 on its fill (known, issue #119).
Decision leading-icon-optional: records that the Textarea has no leading icon (#103 step 15, point 1). No token or rendering change yet.
Decision message-color-error: the error message keeps the functional error text color (a keep decision). No token change.

Decision severity-icon: new part severity-icon and property severityIcon (message by default, after-control, none). New tokens textarea.severity-icon.* (icon font, size 20 / 24 / 24 px after the control, gap space.8, color error the on-base error icon), and in the message textarea.severity-icon.size.message (16 px), textarea.severity-icon.gap.message (space.4).

Decision message-text-size: the message (textarea.message.typography.*) is 14 / 16 / 16 px (body.size.sm, md, md), the label's and the value's size, instead of 12 / 12 / 14. The description is unchanged.

Decision error-fill-subtle: a field in error is filled with global.bg.subtle.functional.error.default (new token textarea.control.background.error), at rest and on hover alike; it kept the page-level fill before. Placeholder on the fill 5.42:1 (light) and 6.62:1 (dark), value 16.91:1 and 11.67:1, the error border against it 5.45:1 and 5.14:1.

Decision variants-modeled-differently (Text field decision of the same name): the departures from the Figma prototype are recorded and read-only is kept. New guideline: a read-only field's fill is 1.05:1 in light and 1.09:1 in dark from the resting fill, the same as the hover fill, so say that it is read-only in the label or the description. The readonly property and the read-only example say so. No token or rendering change.

Decision placeholder-tertiary (Text field decision of the same name): the placeholder (textarea.control.placeholder-color.*) stays global.text.on-base.neutral.tertiary in every enabled state, rather than Figma's secondary at rest. Distance from the value, light / dark: 3.12:1 / 1.76:1 (secondary 1.48:1 / 1.27:1); contrast against the fill at rest 6.08:1 / 6.40:1 (lowest 5.75:1 / 5.86:1). Kept as it was: no token or rendering change.

Decision border-base-neutral-5 (Text field decision of the same name): the resting border of the box (textarea.control.border-color.default) is global.border.base.neutral.5 instead of global.border.accent.neutral.default: #8C8C8C in light (was #313131) and #9C9C9C in dark (was #CFCFCF). Contrast of the border on the surface levels 0 / 1 / 2 / 3: light 3.30 / 3.12 / 3.30 / 3.12:1, dark 6.40 / 5.86 / 5.36 / 4.80:1 (was 12.78 / 12.09 / 12.78 / 12.09:1 and 11.28 / 10.33 / 9.46 / 8.47:1). Disabled, focus and the severities are unchanged.

Decision fill-page-level (Text field decision of the same name): the fill of the box (textarea.control.background.*) stays the page's level, global.bg.level.0.default at rest and .hover on hover, global.bg.level.1.default when read-only. Kept as it was: no token or rendering change.

Decision state-outline-flush: focus is an outline of 2.4 px (focus.ring.width, color.focus.ring) drawn flush over the 0.6 px border, offset minus the border width, instead of a ring 4 px away; a severity (error, warning, success) is an outline of 1.2 px (stroke-width.md) in the severity's border color (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default), 2.4 px in that color with focus; the border and the text never change; outline-offset.focus-visible removed. Contrast, light / dark: focus outline 5.77:1 / 12.76:1 on the default surface (5.45 / 9.58 on level 3); severity outlines as the severity borders, on the default surface and at least on every surface level: error 6.12:1 / 4.97:1 and 5.79 / 3.73, warning 3.27:1 / 8.09:1 and 3.09 / 6.07, success 7.87:1 / 6.08:1 and 7.44 / 4.57. WCAG 2.4.13 is no longer claimed.

Decision radius-button: the corner radius of the box is the Button's at the same size (textarea.control.border-radius per size: small corner-radius.2xs, 2 px; medium and large corner-radius.xs, 4 px; it was corner-radius.xs, 4 px, at every size). Colors, sizes and typography unchanged.

Decision part-gap-6: the parts of the field are 6 px apart at every size and in every state (textarea.container.gap: space.4 to space.6, 4 px to 6 px between the label, the box, the description and the message). The box never moves between states. Colors, sizes and typography unchanged.

Decision label-help-text-sizes (Text field decision of the same name): the label scales with the field (14 / 16 / 16 px) and the help text shrinks (12 / 12 / 14 px) (textarea.label.typography: one 14 px style becomes small, medium and large, font size body.size.sm to sm / md / md, line height normal 1.5 to tight 1.2; textarea.description.typography and textarea.message.typography: body.size.sm to xs / xs / sm, so 14 px becomes 12 / 12 / 14 px; weights, normal line height and letter spacing kept). The Size property now affects the label, the description and the message. pnpm validate now fails when the label and the value alias different font size tokens. Colors unchanged; contrast re-measured on levels 0 to 3: description 12.78:1 (levels 0 and 2) and 12.09:1 (levels 1 and 3) in light mode, 8.86:1, 8.11:1, 7.43:1 and 6.65:1 on levels 0 to 3 in dark mode; error text 6.12:1 and 5.79:1 (levels 0 and 2, then 1 and 3) in light mode, 7.06:1, 6.47:1, 5.92:1 and 5.30:1 in dark mode, the same on every platform; 4.5:1 required (WCAG 1.4.3), the lowest being 6.65:1 (description) and 5.30:1 (error text).

Decision padding-inline-button (Text field decision of the same name): the inline padding (textarea.control.padding-inline.*) is the Button's inline padding without an icon at the same size. Kept as it was: no token or rendering change.

Decision box-height-button (Text field decision of the same name): the minimum height takes the height of the Button of the same size (textarea.control.min-height.*: 32 / 40 / 48 px become 28 / 36 / 44 px). Target size (WCAG 2.5.8): every size stays above 24 x 24 CSS px. Colors unchanged, so contrast is unchanged.

Decision value-text-button-size (Text field decision of the same name): the value and placeholder text takes the text size of the Button of the same size (small 14, medium 16, large 16 px; the large size was 20 px), with the tight line height of the Text field (textarea.control.typography.*: large font size body.size.lg to body.size.md, line height normal to tight). Supersedes sizes. Colors unchanged, so contrast is unchanged.

Decision same-box-as-text-field (Text field decision field-family-mirrors): the Textarea is a mirror of the Text field, so every Text field decision on the box applies here in the same change and pnpm validate compares the tokens; its block padding is declared as its own. No token, CSS or template change: the tokens already resolve to the Text field's values in every platform and mode, so sizes, colors and contrast are unchanged.

Breaking, decision forms-severity: the invalid property is replaced by severity (none, error, warning, success), errorMessage by message and the part error-message by message, the state invalid by error, warning and success; the web attribute data-invalid by data-severity. Tokens: control.border-color.invalid is control.border-color.error, with warning and success and reads the accent functional border (global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default) instead of the base error border; error-message.* is message.*, and message.color.<severity> reads global.text.on-base.functional.<severity>.default. CSS: [data-severity="<severity>"] and [data-state="<severity>"], textarea__error-message is textarea__message. The accent borders reach 3:1 on every surface level since the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1); the light warning border is 2.95:1 on the subtle warning fill, which step 6 may use as the fill, a shortfall the team accepted knowingly (issue #119).

Fix, no decision changed: the Figma library's POC2 export (Color foundation 3.1.0) moves the values of the roles the tokens alias; the tokens, CSS and template are unchanged. Light: 8 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #C01619. Dark: 8 tokens follow the ash retune (one to four units per channel); control.border-color.default reads global.border.accent.neutral.default: #B9B7B7 becomes #CFCFCF; control.border-color.invalid reads global.border.base.functional.error.default: #E12A23 becomes #DF2821; error-message.color reads global.text.on-base.functional.error.default: #EE5248 becomes #F88275. Contrast re-measured on the accessibility guidelines: 3.82 → 3.73:1, 4.26 → 5.79:1, 4.52 → 6.12:1, 4.97 → 7.06:1, 5.79 → 5.77:1, 6.36 → 6.40:1, 11.27 → 11.28:1, 12.14 → 12.09:1, 12.80 → 12.76:1, 12.87 → 12.78:1, 19.07 → 19.03:1.
